entities.summary: Persian mathematician (c. 780–850 CE) from the Abbasid House of Wisdom in Baghdad, whose treatise Al-Jabr wal-Muqabala gave algebra its name and introduced systematic methods for solving linear and quadratic equations. The Latinization of his name gave us the word "algorithm." His work transmitted Hindu-Arabic numerals to Europe, transforming mathematics forever.
